behaviour_summary: pi0 puts the first pot on the stove efficiently (done by ~227), reaches the second pot by ~267, then spends ~170 steps hovering beside it before grasping; it carries it over and is still pressing it down next to pot 1 when the episode times out at 529.

failures.mode_definition: The gripper hovers next to the target and makes repeated small adjustments for many seconds before committing to a grasp, using up the episode time budget.
failures.rl_subtask: pick(moka_pot) from pre-grasp pose and place it on the stove
failures.rl_success_check: second moka pot grasped and lifted within ~60 steps of reset, then resting on the stove cook region with the gripper open
failures.observation: Step 260-273 the open gripper is above-right of the second pot. Steps 287-420 it descends slowly toward the pot's handle/lid side with small back-and-forth corrections and no closure; the fingers close around the pot body only at ~433-447 and the pot lifts at 460. The ~170-step delay leaves too little time for the place: at 487-529 the pot is being lowered beside pot 1 on the stove and is still held at the timeout.

notes: Timeout-driven failure on an in-distribution libero_10 task. The final placement (evidence_pot2_place_at_timeout.png) looks cramped: pot 2 overlaps pot 1 on the stove and may not fit in the cook region even with more time; I did not record it as a separate failure because the episode ends mid-place. At 3 fps the hover phase is clearly visible; at 1 fps it would look like a stall.
